uranium.def: The radioactive metal used as nuclear fuel; reactor fuel is enriched to about 3 to 5 percent uranium-235, the isotope that splits easily.

nuclear-fission.def: The splitting of a heavy nucleus, such as uranium-235, when struck by a neutron, releasing a large amount of heat and more neutrons that can continue a chain reaction.

radioactive-decay.def: The process in which an unstable nucleus gives off radiation and changes into a different element or isotope.

half-life.def: The time it takes for half of the radioactive atoms in a sample to decay; amount left = starting amount × 0.5^(time ÷ half-life).

nuclear-waste.def: Radioactive material left from nuclear power, mainly spent fuel rods, which stays dangerous for thousands of years and must be stored away from people and water.

meltdown.def: Severe overheating of a reactor core after loss of cooling, so the fuel melts and radioactive material may escape, as at Three Mile Island, Chernobyl and Fukushima.
